gloss: to resist; to oppose; to defy

definitions.gloss: to resist; to oppose; to put up resistance
definitions.explanation: To actively fight against or refuse to accept a force, authority, or situation. Can be physical resistance or abstract opposition.

definitions.gloss: to feel reluctant; to have reservations about
definitions.explanation: To feel a psychological aversion or discomfort toward something. Used when something goes against one's feelings or values.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}は{逮捕|たいほ}に{抵抗|ていこう}した。
{市民|しみん}たちは{不当|ふとう}な{法律|ほうりつ}に{抵抗|ていこう}した。
examples.english: The citizens resisted the unjust law.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}まで{抵抗|ていこう}したが、{結局|けっきょく}{降伏|こうふく}するしかなかった。
examples.english: They resisted to the end, but ultimately had no choice but to surrender.

examples.japanese: {虫|むし}を{食|た}べることに{抵抗|ていこう}がある。
examples.english: I have reservations about eating insects.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めは{抵抗|ていこう}があったが、{慣|な}れてきた。
examples.english: I was reluctant at first, but I've gotten used to it.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らない{人|ひと}と{相部屋|あいべや}になることに{抵抗|ていこう}を{感|かん}じる{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people feel reluctant about sharing a room with a stranger.

notes:
PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [force/authority]に{抵抗|ていこう}する (to resist [something] — sense 1)
- [thing]に{抵抗|ていこう}がある (to feel reluctance about [something] — sense 2)

NOUN USAGE:
{抵抗|ていこう} is frequently used as a standalone noun: {抵抗|ていこう}がある (to have reluctance), {抵抗|ていこう}を{感|かん}じる (to feel resistance).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抵抗|ていこう}{運動|うんどう} (resistance movement)
- {抵抗|ていこう}{勢力|せいりょく} (resistance forces)
- {抵抗|ていこう}を{試|こころ}みる (to attempt to resist)
- {抵抗|ていこう}なく (without resistance/reluctance)
